result:
The episode ended at the 34-action budget without a clean recovery. I never got a healthy probe, so `verification_windows` stayed at 0. I haven't seen the final score. The last queries returned "Episode already completed", so I can't inspect the sidecar further.

What I fixed:
- **Checkin consumer:** I re-enabled it and set `auto_pause_after_attempts` to 0. I restarted the checkin worker and replayed the backlog. Every valid event is delivered, with 0 pending.
- **Corrupt event:** One outbox event had a truncated payload and kept failing with "expected object". I quarantined `evt_00000395_…`, the only quarantined event. Its booking was already confirmed, and I didn't check whether a check-in row exists for it.
- **Stuck bookings:**
  - `bkg_1196…`, `bkg_b40c…` and `bkg_cdab…` already had captured charges, so I confirmed each against its existing charge.
  - `bkg_855e…` was a duplicate of the same `client_reference`. I voided it, which refunded 25000 cents.
  - `bkg_beae…` was declined at the provider, so I voided it. That used 1 of the 3 provider lookups.
- **Payment timeouts:** I raised `payment_timeout_ms` from 200 to 2000.
- **Pricing cache:** I disabled it and cleared it, after the booking logs showed repeated "stale pricing quote" 409s.

What was still wrong:
- All six probes came back unhealthy. The last booking logs still showed "stale pricing quote" 409s. I couldn't tell whether those were old entries or new ones, so I don't know the cause. Disabling and clearing the cache didn't visibly fix it.
- Each probe can only count after the last mutation. I was spending actions on reads and probes to diagnose this, and they ran out.

I didn't call `finish`. The budget ending should have triggered the receipt, but I haven't checked that `episode.json` contains it.

I spent actions on separate reads and on repeated probes without a diagnosis. A single query of the `flights` and `cache` tables and the pricing logs, right after the first stale-quote sighting, would have been cheaper.
